findings.title: Invalid free
findings.body:
`transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags` is set to `&config.features`. That set is a field embedded in the JSBundler `Config`, not a block from `allocator.create`.

`BundleOptions.deinit` frees any pointer that is not the static empty set by calling `deinit()` and then `allocator.destroy()`. If this transpiler is deinitialized, Bun would:
- destroy memory it never allocated; and
- double-free the set when `Config.deinit` later calls `self.features.deinit()`.

The pointer overwrite also leaks any set already allocated by `fromApi` from `transform.feature_flags`.

The same ownership problem applies to transpiler copies that share the pointer and are each deinitialized. Not verified from this diff: whether `Transpiler.deinit` actually runs for the `Bun.build` transpiler. The consequence would be memory corruption, so ownership should be made explicit, for example with an `owned` flag or by always cloning the set.

findings.title: Shared-pointer free
findings.body:
`deinit` unconditionally destroys `bundler_feature_flags` whenever it is not the empty sentinel. The same pointer is copied into `opts.features` for every parse and is assigned from external owners, such as the JSBundler config.

Any `BundleOptions` or `Transpiler` that is struct-copied (for example, for worker or child transpilers) and later deinitialized will free the shared set more than once.

findings.title: Stale runtime cache
findings.body:
`bundler_feature_flags` changes the transpiled output, but it is not included in `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`. The runtime transpiler cache is keyed on those fields.

Trigger: run `bun run --feature=X file.ts` on a file large enough to be cached, then run `bun run file.ts` without the flag. The second run can reuse cached output that still has `feature("X")` replaced with `true`.

The enabled flag set, for example a hash of the sorted flags, should be part of the cache key.
